question: Which of the following are the end products of respiration in plants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CO2, H2O and Energy.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Respiration **is a process by which living organisms release energy from food molecules such as glucose.
 
• In plants, respiration occurs in mitochondria, which are organelles present in the cells.
 
• During respiration, **glucose is broken down **into smaller molecules such as pyruvate, which then undergo a series of chemical reactions **to produce CO2, water, and energy.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Respiration in Roots:**

 
• The plant's underground portion, the roots, take in air from the spaces and air gaps between the soil particles.
 
• The **oxygen that is taken up by the roots is used to release energy**, which is then employed to move minerals and salts out of the soil.
 
• This is the reason we frequently hear people warn against spending the night beneath a tree because the excess carbon dioxide that trees release after they breathe can cause **asphyxia.**

**Respiration in Stems:**

 
• In order for the stem to breathe, air diffuses into the stomata and travels through various cell regions.
 
• The released carbon dioxide is also dispersed via the stomata at this point.
 
• **Gaseous exchange is known to occur in lenticels **in woody or higher plants.

**Respiration in Leaves:**

 
• The minuscule openings in leaves are called stomata.
 
• **Every stomata is regulated by guard cells.**
 
• When the stoma between the inferior leaf and the atmosphere closes and opens, gases are exchanged.
